task.title: Bound the cost of large --all-options runs and fetch every option set
task.problem: Each option set is a full project load, but --all-options gave no estimate of the time a large --max-option-sets would take, kept every set's element graph in memory until the end (about 9.5 MB per set on a 500-element project), built every set up front, and required a manual bst source fetch per combination.
task.proposal: Generate option sets lazily, record trees right after each load and release that set's element graph, print a time estimate after the first set and periodic progress, and add an explicit --fetch-sources that fetches (never tracks) each set before loading it.
acceptance: Memory no longer grows with each option set when --origin is not used; option sets are not materialized up front.
With more than one option set, a note after the first set estimates the remaining time and is refreshed at most every 30 seconds.
--fetch-sources fetches each option set's selected sources and junctions before loading it; nothing is fetched without it and sources are never tracked.
evidence: 500-element project, 128 option sets: peak RSS 1268 MB before, 212 MB after; about 2.8 s per set.
test_progress_estimates_remaining_option_sets and the --fetch-sources run in test_all_options_searches_union_of_option_sets pass against BuildStream 2.8.1.
